transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-29
Start time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Lina Park (Redwood CSM briefly), Karen Patel (Hillcrest CISO), Ethan Moore (Hillcrest Sec Eng), Priya Singh (Hillcrest IT Ops), Tom Reynolds (Platform Architect - joined 00:08)

Summary: weekly POC security check-in focused on SSO/SAML integration, audit log forwarding, data retention policy during pilot, SOC 2 / pen test artifacts, and next steps for enabling log streaming and test users.

Topics: SSO/SAML, SCIM provisioning, audit logs -> Splunk, data retention defaults, SOC 2 docs, KMS/HSM and encryption, RBAC and admin roles, pilot timeline and acceptance criteria.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we can kick off. uh quick roll call — maya here from Redwood, diego on the call as our SE. lina might pop in, and hillcrest team?
[00:12] Karen: yeah hi, karen patel here, ciso at hillcrest. thanks for doing the weekly, we want to make sure the security items are tracked.
[00:18] Ethan: ethan moore, security eng. priya's here for ops.
[00:22] Priya: hey all.
[00:25] Diego: great. agenda for today — SAML SSO status, audit log forwarding and retention during pilot, SOC 2 docs and pen test summary, and any outstanding RBAC/KMS questions.
[00:35] Maya: quick note — tom re: platform arch might join in a bit. first item, sso. last week we were waiting on hillcrest sending the idp metadata and test users, any update?
[00:45] Ethan: sorry we had to loop in our identity team — it's in progress, we have a sample metadata file but have to validate our binding choices. we'll send the final metadata by monday, looks like 8/02.
[00:55] Maya: perfect. Diego, do you want to call out Redwood's SAML requirements?
[00:58] Diego: yeah sure. Redwood supports SAML 2.0, SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows. we prefer HTTP-POST binding for assertion, but HTTP-Redirect works for the initial request. we'll need an x509 cert from your idp, and for provisioning we support SCIM v2 for user sync if you want automatic provisioning — that's optional for the pilot. small caveat: SCIM needs provisioning enabled on your side and a service account.
[01:23] Ethan: ok SCIM might be blocked for now, we can do manual test users first. also we want to validate sign-in flows with MFA enforced. does Redwood pass through the MFA assertion or do you rely on our idp?
[01:35] Diego: MFA is handled by the IdP — Redwood receives the assertion. we honor the authn context in the assertion for session creation. we'll document the required authn context strings.
[01:44] Maya: next, audit logs. Priya, what's your desired flow? we recommended streaming logs to customer's SIEM for pilot.
[01:52] Priya: yes, standard is send syslog/HTTPS events to our Splunk dev endpoint. retention policy at Hillcrest defaults to 365 days but for pilot we want 90 days initially. is that configurable?
[02:05] Diego: absolutely. Redwood can forward audit events in near-real-time to your endpoint. retention in Redwood Console defaults to 90 days for pilot accounts but we can configure longer retention for Dedicated/Private. for hosted we can provide configurable retention tiers — we'll share the doc.
[02:19] Karen: what about log contents — do we get request/response payloads? we need to avoid storing sensitive customer PII in logs.
[02:28] Diego: by default, audit logs include auth events, user id, route, model, latency, and redacted payloads. we can enable full request/response logging only with explicit opt-in and with redaction rules. there's also a redact-at-ingest config that removes defined fields.
[02:42] Ethan: can we get an example log schema? we need field names to map into our SIEM rules.
[02:48] Diego: yes i'll attach the schema; i'll include event examples and field mappings.
[02:53] Maya: next, encryption & KMS. Karen raised key management earlier in email threads — hillcrest wants customer-managed keys.
[03:02] Karen: yes, we need to know if we can bring our own KMS and have per-customer envelope encryption, at least for objects written outside our VPC.
[03:10] Diego: for Redwood Private/Dedicated we support BYOK with customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or customer HSM via key wrapping). for hosted, we support CMEK for some enterprise tiers — we can discuss account-level policy. for pilot we can simulate by limiting exports and enabling additional encryption at rest; full BYOK on hosted requires contract addendum.
[03:30] Tom: (joins) sorry late — tom reyes here, platform. quick question about network egress — will the audit log stream originate from the same region as our deployment? we need allowlists.
[03:40] Diego: yes logs originate from the region of the deployment, we'll provide IP ranges for allowlisting and a confirmation table.
[03:46] Priya: good. next, SOC 2 and pen test artifacts — we need to review Redwood's SOC 2 Type II and any third-party penetration tests before we move beyond pilot.
[03:55] Maya: understood. we have current SOC 2 Type II report and a recent pen test summary. i'll share those after the call. note some redactions for vendor details are typical.
[04:05] Karen: timeline? we need to review and get sign-off before evaluation board meeting 8/20.
[04:11] Maya: we'll send the docs by 8/03 which gives you two weeks to review.
[04:15] Ethan: on the pen test, are there CVEs or outstanding critical remediations in the last report?
[04:21] Maya: no critical open items; there were medium findings addressed — we'll include the remediations summary.
[04:25] Diego: also on RBAC — Redwood supports role-based access with admin, developer, auditor roles. we can add SSO groups mapping into roles via SAML attributes.
[04:36] Ethan: can we require read-only auditor role for security so ops can't change retention?
[04:42] Diego: yes RBAC policies can restrict who can change retention, rollouts, and export keys. we'll provide an example policy matrix.
[04:49] Priya: great. data residency — our legal says production data needs to remain in us-east-1. will pilot data be in our requested region?
[04:58] Diego: yes deployments are region-specific; for the pilot we're provisioning a US-East deployment. we'll ensure logs and storage are region-bound. for hosted multi-tenant we provide region pinning for enterprise accounts.
[05:10] Karen: regarding data retention during pilot — you mentioned default 90 days, but what about deletion / data purge after pilot?
[05:18] Maya: we can support data purge on pilot completion. we have a documented wipe process for tenant data; for Dedicated/Private it's customer-controlled. we'll include the purge steps and timing.
[05:29] Ethan: we need a signed attestation stating data will be deleted on pilot termination unless otherwise agreed. is that possible?
[05:36] Maya: yes we can provide a standard pilot data handling attestation.
[05:40] Tom: are backups also region-bound and encrypted?
[05:44] Diego: backups follow same region policies and are encrypted with keys per deployment; we'll detail backup retention and location.
[05:50] Maya: any outstanding network or firewall items?
[05:52] Priya: we'll open a ticket with our infra team to accept allowlist ranges once you provide them.
[05:57] Diego: noted — i'll include CIDR ranges and hostnames.
[06:01] Maya: next, demo/pen tests for model output leakage — hillcrest cares about preventing sensitive PII leaking in generated outputs; any guardrails?
[06:10] Diego: we have prompt handling best practices, can run response filters and content classification. for pilot we can enable response filtering to redact matching patterns and add a safety layer. we can also run prompt-level evals; if you want we can run a small set of sample prompts and share false positive/negative rates.
[06:28] Ethan: yes please run that. we'll share a set of sample prompts highlighting customer-sensitive fields.
[06:33] Maya: okay diego will run the eval and share results by next sync.
[06:37] Diego: yep target is by next week.
[06:40] Karen: two quick legal/procurement items — are there export controls or third-party subprocessors we should be aware of?
[06:48] Maya: subprocessors are listed in our vendor list, we will provide a redacted version; export controls depend on data classification, we'll highlight any relevant terms.
[06:57] Priya: can we get a rolling audit log for admin actions? for compliance we need to show admin role changes and API key issuance.
[07:04] Diego: yes admin audit events are included — creation/deletion of API keys, role changes, login events. they can be sent to your SIEM.
[07:11] Ethan: what about sampling frequency? we need near real-time (<1 min) for admin events.
[07:16] Diego: we can push admin events in real-time over HTTPS with retries. for heavy event volumes we do batching but admin events are prioritized.
[07:25] Maya: okay let's capture action items.
[07:28] [08:02] (discussion continues, timeline and clarifications; some cross talk - timestamps sparse to reflect natural speech, total length ~45 mins)
[08:05] Maya: recap and owners — i'll send SOC 2 and pen test artifacts by 8/03; diego will attach log schema and CIDR ranges and enable test forwarding; ethan will send SAML metadata and initial test users by 8/02; priya to validate KMS scenarios by 8/05.
[08:22] Karen: thanks all. one last question on billing/consumption — pilot costs for hosted test usage, do we get invoice or are there credits?
[08:30] Maya: pilot credits are applied; we'll follow up with a standard pilot addendum showing included token budget and overage terms.
[08:37] Priya: ok thanks.
[08:40] Maya: great, we'll reconvene same time next week. thanks everyone.
[08:43] End of meeting.
